title: Canonical finite intrinsic comparison preserves tensor generators
statement: Let X be a scheme and A a commutative ring. The canonical comparison from fixed-A-module sheaves on the small etale site to intrinsic module sheaves over the constant ring on the pro-etale site admits a natural tensor isomorphism. Its map from the comparison of M tensor N to the tensor of the comparisons sends every sheaf tensor of local etale sections x,y, mapped through both adjunction units, to the intrinsic sheaf tensor of the images of x and y. There is no flatness, constructibility or nonempty-site hypothesis.

proof.text: Use the strong monoidal comparison inverse image on fixed-module sheaves. Its adjunction tensor identity and the tensor formula for the continuous restriction functor show that its comonoidal map sends the image of each etale pure tensor to the pure tensor of the images.

Encode constant-module presheaves as module presheaves; sectionwise tensor gives a natural isomorphism by the identity on pure tensors. Scalar module sheafification along the constant-ring unit preserves locally bijective maps, as seen by forgetting to additive sheafification. In particular it inverts the lax tensor map of ordinary sheaf inclusion: that map is adjoint to the invertible ordinary sheafification tensor comparison and counits.

Compose the natural module-sheafification tensor isomorphism, the sectionwise encoding isomorphism and the inverted inclusion tensor map to obtain the tensor isomorphism for intrinsic realization. Naturality of the module sheafification unit and the supplied pure-tensor formula determine its value on generators. Compose with the comparison from step 1. Naturality of the two units gives the claimed formula.
